name: North Dakota

context: ND 340: for spring erosion control before seeding sugar beets, 10-20 pounds/acre of barley has shown to be adequate.
ND 603: herbaceous wind barriers need a minimum expected height of 1.5 feet and porosity of 40 to 50 percent.
ND 380: the protected zone is 10H on the leeward side and 2H on the windward side.
cover_rules: ND 340: to protect an establishing cash crop, design the cover crop to reduce wind erosion to less than 0.5 ton per acre in the critical period.
ND 340: 1,420 lbs/ac of biomass is a good target level for erosion control.
ND 340: bulk seed must be a minimum of 85% germination; below that, base the rate on PLS.
residue: ND 329: maintain a minimum of 60 percent residue cover on the soil surface throughout the year.
ND 329: the crop interval STIR value shall be no greater than 20.
ND 329: residue should not be shredded after harvest; shredding makes it more susceptible to movement by wind or water.
barriers: ND 603: barrier spacing must not exceed 10 times the planned barrier height; run barriers perpendicular to prevailing wind.
ND 603: within row spacing must not be greater than 36 inches wide; use erect plants with stiff stems.
ND 603: reestablish gaps in barriers (e.g., 10-15 feet) as soon as practical.
windbreak: ND 380: the interval between windbreaks must not exceed that permitted by the soil loss tolerance (T).
ND 380: select species taller than the crop; orient the windbreak perpendicular to the wind.
grazing: ND 528: keep enough plant cover, litter and trampled plant residue to limit soil movement by wind and water.
ND 528: grazed cover crops and annual forages need 6-8 inches minimum stubble.
drought: ND 528: under drought conditions, recovery periods may need to be extended to 90 days or longer.
seeding: ND herbaceous guide: seeding dates may vary plus or minus 5 days if justified by moisture and temperature conditions.
ND herbaceous guide: late fall (dormant) seeding may begin once soil temperatures are 40 degrees Fahrenheit or less for a minimum of 5 consecutive days.
ND 342: shape steep edges of sand blowouts to one (1) foot vertical to five (5) feet horizontal, or flatter.
disturbed: ND 342: stabilize areas with existing or expected high rates of soil erosion by wind or water.
dunes: ND 342: for sand dunes, shape steep edges of sand blowouts to one (1) foot vertical to five (5) feet horizontal, or flatter.
ND 342: for a woody planting, consider using anchored mulch.

cover.name: Barley
cover.rate: 10-20 pounds/acre for spring erosion control before sugar beets

coverPlant.text: ND 340: if seeding between August 20th and September 5th, include winter annual species in the mix.
ND 340: after early harvested wheat, barley, canola and flax, seed a full rate cover crop and allow frost termination.

seedWin.text: ND herbaceous guide: cool-season species in spring, prior to May 20 (north) or prior to May 10 (south).
ND herbaceous guide: cool-season species in late summer, August 10 to September 1 (north) or August 10 to September 15 (south).
ND herbaceous guide: warm-season species in spring, May 10 to June 25.
